taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: stems 3-4 dm. high, floccose-woolly.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: a stem with its head rarely over 50 cm, just over Abrams and Ferris's 3-4 dm.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: from a perennial or biennial base; drawn as a perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: woolly herbs.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: the basal leaves persisting, the stem leaves few and toward the base.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: stem leaves few, mostly near the base, smaller than the basal.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Stem leaves alternate, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: leaves pinnatifid to entire: simple blades, often deeply cut.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: leaves pinnatifid to entire; the basal ones of this species pinnately parted or lobed in the photos.

traits.division_pattern.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: leaves pinnatifid.

traits.division_order.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: leaves pinnatifid: cut once.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: basal leaves 3 cm to 8 cm long including the stalk, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 1.5 cm to 4 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Basal blades ovate to obovate in outline, pinnately cut, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Lobes entire, rounded, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: floccose-woolly throughout.

traits.hair_colour.note: Wool white, giving the plant a silver-grey look; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: heads solitary on peduncles 1-3 dm. long.

traits.inflorescence_unit.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: heads long-peduncled.

traits.peduncle_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: peduncles 1-3 dm. long.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: rays bright yellow, 25-50.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: involucre 7-8 mm. high.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: involucre 11-16 mm. broad.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: rays 25-50.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 196, Baileya multiradiata: ligules 11-15 mm. long.

traits.ray_colour.note: Rays bright lemon yellow, papery and reflexed in age; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.disc_colour.note: Disc deep yellow; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 148404358, 106628792, 72916633, 140306081, 158777342, 212945763, 161642925, 18473959): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.pappus.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya: pappus none.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a cypsela without pappus.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cypselae 3 mm to 4 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya multiradiata: up to 5,000 feet, very common on sandy plains and mesas and along roadsides, March to October (Abrams and Ferris 1960 p. 196: April to October).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cypselae ripen from April to November, a month behind the flowers.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya multiradiata: up to 5,000 feet: about 1,520 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya multiradiata: sandy plains and mesas, in the open.

traits.soil_texture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 970), Baileya multiradiata: sandy plains and mesas.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a silvery woolly clump of pinnately cut basal leaves sending up many slender grey stems, each ending in one bright yellow daisy with papery rays.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for desert marigold from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of Oregon sunshine (eriophyllum-lanatum); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.35 m tall at 3 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
